title: Realizations and dynamics of shared-resource mass-action systems
abstract: Ordinary mass-action realizations are characterized for a finite family of two-species modules coupled through a shared resource and buffer. Every positive parameter vector admits a strongly connected realization of the same polynomial field. A complex-balanced realization at a prescribed positive state exists exactly when the state is stationary and two explicit local flux inequalities hold, even when arbitrary finite auxiliary complexes on the same species are allowed. An explicit endpoint sign test determines the untransported heterogeneous parameter locus, and the state criterion extends to directed transfers of both private species. A homogeneous specialization has the sharp sharing threshold v <= n/8, including equality. Global positive solutions and permanence uniform over compact sets of initial conditions are established. For d >= 1, the positive equilibrium is unique and is locally exponentially stable in the homogeneous family. Complex-balanced realizations yield global convergence, including with transport, and local exponential stability is established for the transported complex-balanced family. An exact example at d = 1/10 has three positive equilibria, two locally exponentially stable and one unstable.
